This appeal coming on for admission this day, the court passe  ORDER Heard on I.A.No.7566/2018, an application under Section 5 of Limitation Act for condonation of delay of 78 days in filing the appeal.
The application is supported by an affidavit.
Considering the averments mentioned in the application, which is supported by an affidavit, the application is allowed and delay in filing the appeal is hereby condoned.

Accordingly, I.A.No.7566/2018 is disposed of.
Heard on the admission.
Admit.
With the consent of parties, heard finally.

The appellant/claimant has filed this Appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 for enhancement of the compensation amount being aggrieved with the award dated 21/11/2017 passed by XIth Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jabalpur (M.P.) in MACC No.43/2015,
by which the learned Claims Tribunal awarded a total sum of Rs.5,17,514/- (Five lakhs seventeen thousand five hundred fourteen) which is rounded off as Rs.5,18,000/- (Five lakhs eighteen thousand) with 6% interest to the appellant/claimant by way of compensation for the injuries, which he has sustained in a motor vehicle accident.
2.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: According to claimant i.e. appellant herein, the compensation awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal is on lower side and hence, need to be enhanced.

3. Since, this appeal is for the enhancement in the compensation amount awarded by the Claims Tribunal, hence the question that arises for consideration is whether any case for enhancement in compensation awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal on facts and evidence adduced, is made out Dheeraj Singh Thakur vs Bahadur Prasad Vishwakarma on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40060641/
2 and if so to what extent?
4. It is not necessary to narrate the entire facts in detail, such as how the accident occurred, who was negligent in driving the offending vehicle, who is liable for paying compensation etc.

sentences.text: It is for the reason that firstly all these findings are recorded in favour of appellant/claimant by the Tribunal.

Secondly, the findings though recorded in favour of claimant is not under challenge at the instance of any of the respondents such as owner/driver or insurance company either by way of filing an appeal or cross-objection.
In this view of the matter, there is no justification to burden this order by detailing facts on all these issues.

5. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that in a motor accident which took place on 21/11/2014 the appellant sustained multiple injuries including grievous injury in his right leg, due to which his right leg was amputated above the knee and learned Tribunal has awarded only a sum of Rs.5,17,514/- (Five lakhs seventeen thousand five hundred fourteen) which is rounded off as Rs.5,18,000/- (Five lakhs eighteen thousand) breakup of which is as under :
Rs.2,04,000/- Towards loss of income due to permanent disability including future prospects Rs.2,16,514/- Towards medical expenses Rs.25,000/- Towards pain and suffering Rs.10,000/- Towards attendant and special diet Rs.12,000/- Towards loss of income during treatment (three months) Rs.50,000/- Towards artificial limb 6.

Learned counsel for the appellant further submits that the Claims Tribunal has assessed the income of appellant/injured @ Rs.4,250/- (Four thousand two hundred fifty) per month, which is on lower side.
The alleged accident is of the year 2014, therefore, as per Minimum Wages Act the income of the appellant ought to have been assessed as Rs.5,845/- (Five thousand eight hundred forty five) per month.

Learned counsel further submits that due to motorcycle accident right leg of the appellant was amputated, due to which he suffered 75% permanent disability and in this regard disability certificate (Ex.P/85) has been filed and Dr. Sharad Dwivedi (AW-3) was examined, who has categorically stated in Para-2 of his statement that appellant sustained 75% permanent disability in his right leg in the alleged incident.
However, the Tribunal has wrongly assessed the permanent disability of whole body as 25% in Para-22 of impugned award.

It is submitted that the appellant was agriculturist and after the incident appellant is not able to do the agricultural work, therefore, at least 40% permanent disability of the whole body ought to have been assessed.
In this regad learned counsel placed reliance on the judgment passed by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarnam Singh Vs. Shriram General Insurance Co. Ltd. & Others, 2023 LiveLaw (SC) 498.

entities.text: Sarnam Singh Vs. Shriram General Insurance Co. Ltd. & Others, 2023 LiveLaw (SC) 498
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel further submitted that the learned Tribunal has not assessed the future prospect of the appellant, while keeping in view the law laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi & others, (2017) 16 SCC 680, 40% should be added towards future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi & others, (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is submitted that on other heads also amount awarded by the learned Tribunal is on lower side, hence it is prayed that the appeal be allowed and amount of compensation be enhanced substantially.
7.

Per contra, learned counsel for respondents opposed the prayer by contending that Dr. Sharad Dwivedi (AW-3), who has issued the permanent disability certificate (Ex.P-85) himself has stated Dheeraj Singh Thakur vs Bahadur Prasad Vishwakarma on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40060641/
3 that the permanent disability of 75% was of a particular limb i.e. right leg and not of whole body, so the learned Tribunal has rightly assessed the permanent disability as 25% of the whole body.

entities.text: Dheeraj Singh Thakur vs Bahadur Prasad Vishwakarma
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel further submits that the learned Tribunal has awarded sufficient amount to the appellant after appreciating all the oral and documentary evidence placed on record.
Hence, he prayed for dismissal of appeal.
8. I have heard the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
9. From perusal of impugned award it appears that the learned Tribunal assessed the income of appellant as Rs.4,250/- (Four thousand two hundred fifty) per month, which appears to be on lower side.

The alleged incident is of the year 2014, so looking to the oral and documentary evidence available in this regard, the income of the appellant is assessed as Rs.5,800/- (Five thousand eight hundred) per month.
10.
So far as permanent disability is concerned, in the alleged incident appellant suffered grievous injuries in his right leg, due to which his right leg was amputated above the knee.
Learned Tribunal in Para-22 of the impugned award assessed the permanent disability as 25%.
In support of his pleadings, appellant/claimant has filed permanent disability certificate (Ex.P/85).

So, looking to the nature of injuries sustained by appellant in the alleged incident and also keeping in view the law laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarnam Singh (supra) permanent disability should be assessed as 40%.

11. It also appears from the record that learned Tribunal has not considered the future prospects of appellant, while as per the law laid down by Hon'ble Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi & ors (2017) 16 SCC 680, 40% of the assessed income is to be added towards future prospect.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi & ors (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 12. At the time of incident the appellant was aged about 34-35 years, therefore, keeping in view the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma Vs. DTC, 2009 (6) SCC 121 multiplier of 16 has rightly been applied by the learned Tribunal.

13. Thus, considering the monthly income of the appellant @ Rs.5,800/- (Five thousand eight hundred) per month, 40% of the assessed income is to be added towards future loss of income,
which comes to Rs.8,120/- (Eight thousand one hundred twenty).
So, the yearly income comes to Rs.97,440/- (Ninety seven thousand four hundred forty).
As discussed above, permanent disability of appellant/claimant is assessed as 40%, so the figure comes to Rs.38,976/- (thirty eight thousand nine hundred seventy six).

Thus, the amount towards loss of income due to permanent disability including future prospects after applying multiplier of 16 comes to Rs.6,23,616/- (Six lakhs twenty three thousand six hundred sixteen).

14. It also appears from the impugned award that learned Tribunal has not awarded any amount to the appellant/claimant in the head of grievous injury and has only awarded a sum of Rs.25,000/-
towards pain and suffering, whereas looking to the injuries caused to the appellant in the alleged Dheeraj Singh Thakur vs Bahadur Prasad Vishwakarma on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40060641/
4 incident, amount should also be awarded in the head of physical and mental suffering, mental shock and grievous injury.

entities.text: Dheeraj Singh Thakur vs Bahadur Prasad Vishwakarma
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So, keeping in view the nature of injury sustained by appellant in the alleged incident and the fact that the right leg of the appellant was amputated below the knee, in my considered opinion a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (One lakh) will be just and proper to be awarded in the head of physical and mental suffering, mental shock and grievous injury.
Similarly, no amount has been awarded by the learned Tribunal in the head of transport expenses, which should be awarded.
Hence, a sum of Rs.5,000/- (Five thousand) is awarded in the head of transport expenses.

15. In view of above discussion, appellant/claimant shall be entitled for the following amount of compensation :-
Rs.6,23,616/-

Towards loss of income due to permanent disability including future prospects Rs.2,16,514/- Towards medical expenses Rs.1,00,000/- Towards physical and mental suffering, mental shock and grievous injury Rs.10,000/- Towards attendant and special diet Rs.17,400/- Towards loss of income during treatment (three months) Rs.50,000/- Towards artificial limb Rs.5,000/- Towards transport expenses
16. Thus the appellant/claimant will be entitled for a total sum of Rs.10,22,530/- (Ten lakhs twenty two thousand five hundred thirty) instead of Rs.5,18,000/- (Five lakhs eighteen thousand).

Thus,
there shall be enhancement to the tune of Rs.5,04,530/- (Five lakhs four thousand five hundred thirty), which shall fetch interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing of claim petition till the date of actual payment except the period of delay of 78 days in filing of the appeal.
The enhanced amount be paid within 60 days from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
Other terms and condition of the award shall remain intact.

17. It is pertinent to mention here that the appellant has valued the appeal as Rs.5,00,000/- (Five lakhs) and paid the Court fee as per valuation, therefore, appellant is directed to pay the Court fees on additional amount of Rs.4,530/- (Four thousand five hundred thirty) also within a period of 30 days from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.

If the Court fee is not paid within the stipulated period, then this order will be restricted only up to the amount of Rs.5,00,000/- (Five lakhs).
18.
With the aforesaid, appeal stands disposed of.
19. Records of the learned Tribunal be sent back alongwith the copy of this order for information and necessary compliance.
